evidence_items.publisher: Stanford Digital Economy Lab (Brynjolfsson, Chandar, Chen)

receipt.public_excerpt:
(1) We find no evidence of widespread, economy-wide
job displacement. (2) However, employment of young workers (ages 22–25) in AI-exposed
occupations now stands 19% below where it would be had it kept pace with that of their
less-exposed peers; experienced workers show no comparable gap.

evidence_items.explanation: Points both ways. No economy-wide displacement fits Zitron's view. A 19% employment gap for young workers in AI-exposed jobs points to some change. The authors call the evidence descriptive, so it is not decisive.

receipt.public_excerpt: “The picture of AI’s impact on the labor market that emerges from our data is one that largely reflects stability, not major disruption at an economy-wide level.”

evidence_items.explanation: Yale Budget Lab found no major economy-wide disruption by early 2026. That fits the forecast so far, but its authors stress that this could change, so it does not settle a forecast with no deadline.

unresolved_gaps: Whether generative AI caused the gap for young workers is not yet established; pre-trends and other explanations are still debated.
No deadline, so continued stability cannot confirm the forecast.
